title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is settling the terminology and set-theoretic bookkeeping for 'ateliers' (until now called 'magasins'; the next page renames the axioms Mag 1-4 to At 1-4). The model case is the atelier M = Figil(L) of figures built from multistrata on a base set L. The elements X of M are called 'strates'. Each X determines the set X̃ of its sub-strata (incident strata), called the 'multistrate' of X.

This page is a typing remark.
- In the model Figil(L), a stratum (déploiement) X is an element of a special kind of P(P(L)), i.e. a set of subsets of L.
- Its multistrate X̃ is a set of such strata, so 'in good logic' it is an element of P(P(P(L))).
- As M becomes the privileged base set, a figure F should simply be a subset of M, i.e. a set of strata. From that viewpoint F̃ (the set of strata incident to F) is just F itself. So there is no point in speaking of 'déploiements' of a figure.
- Usage will show whether F should later be made autonomous from M. That would mean a mixed structure on the pair (M, F) with an incidence relation (the drawn triangle, probably the incidence symbol ⊴ of the next page) between M and F. In that case F̃ would regain its meaning.

In modern terms: this is a choice between two encodings of an incidence structure. One treats figures as down-closed subsets (order ideals) of a poset of strata. The other treats points and figures as two sorts linked by an incidence relation, as in a two-sorted incidence geometry or a bipartite incidence structure.

Purpose: to fix a clean formalism for a combinatorial or 'tame' stratified geometry of figures, the 'ateliers' of 1986. The next page defines supports ('contours') Σ_A ⊂ P(A), closed under arbitrary intersections, from the relations ⊴, the closure relation written ≪ with a small circle above it, and a symmetric non-reflexive relation |∘|.
errors: No mathematical errors. The page is a type-level remark that is internally consistent: if strata live in P(P(L)), multistrata live in P(P(P(L))). The phrase 'déploiement X' in the first line and 'strate' on the previous page refer to the same objects, so the terminology is still in flux.

ideas.what: Set-theoretic typing of strata and multistrata in the model atelier Figil(L): strata are elements of P(P(L)), multistrata are elements of P(P(P(L))).
Figures as subsets of the privileged base set M of strata, so that F̃ = F and 'déploiements' of figures are unnecessary.
ideas.modern_name: figures as order ideals / down-sets in a poset of strata (cf. subcomplexes of a face poset)

ideas.what: Possible future 'mixed structure' on (M, F) with an incidence relation between strata and figures, making figures autonomous.
ideas.modern_name: two-sorted incidence structure / bipartite incidence geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical incidence geometry (Hilbert; Buekenhout, Tits for incidence geometries)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely terminological and set-theoretic housekeeping page within the unpublished 1986 'ateliers' project. The project as a whole (axiomatic ateliers of strata and figures) is little known. This page itself contains no substantive result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The page number at top is '36', not '38' (the previous page is 35, the next is 37); '39' at the bottom left is the archive folio number.
'une multi-structure X̃' should read 'une multistrate X̃'.
'sy[?] élément' is likely a struck or abbreviated 'un élément'.
The symbol before 'entre M et F' is a drawn triangle, most likely the incidence relation symbol (cf. ⊴ on the next page), not Δ.
In the first line, 'de 𝓜' refers to M, i.e. the atelier M = Figil(L).
